title: sin i against sin r gives the refractive index
caption: Snell's law for light entering the block from air is sin i = n sin r, so a graph of sin i against sin r is a straight line through the origin whose gradient is n. A gradient of 1.48 identifies the block as Perspex/acrylic (crown glass would give about 1.52).
alt: Graph of sin i against sin r: a straight line through the origin with gradient 1.48, passing through (0.60, 0.888).
description: The horizontal axis is sin r (angle of refraction in the block) and the vertical axis is sin i (angle of incidence in air).
Because sin i = n sin r, the points lie on a straight line through the origin with gradient n = 1.48.
For example sin r = 0.60 corresponds to sin i = 0.888.
A gradient of 1.48 matches Perspex; glass at 1.52 would be a slightly steeper line.
